grammar.title: 數字 + 量詞 + 名詞（位、條、種）
grammar.pattern: Number / 這·那 / 幾 + Measure Word + Noun
grammar.explanation: In Chinese a number can never sit directly in front of a noun; you need a measure word in between. 位 is the polite measure word for people (老師、先生、小姐、客人). 條 is for long, thin things (路、魚、河). 種 means 'kind / type' (兩種茶、這種手機). The same slot works after 這／那／幾: 這條路, 那位小姐, 幾種菜. For money, note that Chinese counts in 萬 (10,000): 20,000 is 兩萬, not 'twenty thousand' word-by-word.
grammar.contrast: 位 vs 個: both count people, but 位 is polite and is used for guests, teachers, customers; 個 is neutral or casual (三個朋友, 一個小孩). In a restaurant the staff always say 幾位, never 幾個人 to your face.
grammar.common_error: Learners either drop the measure word ('三老師', '兩魚') or stack words wrongly and say 三個位／兩位人. Say 三位老師, 兩條魚, 我們四位. Also, for big money amounts learners translate 'ten thousand' as 十千 — it must be 一萬.

passage.title: 市場的一天
passage.hanzi: 週末我跟妹妹去了一家很大的市場。那裡有很多種東西，水果、魚、花，什麼都有。我們先買了兩條魚，又買了一些花，準備放在家裡的桌上。有一位老闆很客氣，還送我們一個蘋果。那天我們花了快一千塊，可是一點也不覺得貴。回家的時候，捷運上人很多，我們站了三十分鐘才到家。
passage.gloss: On the weekend my little sister and I went to a big market. There are all kinds of things there — fruit, fish, flowers, everything. First we bought two fish, then some flowers to put on the table at home. One shop owner was very friendly and even gave us an apple. That day we spent nearly a thousand NT, but I didn't feel it was expensive at all. On the way home the MRT was crowded, and we stood for thirty minutes before we got home.

grammar.title: 完成 (finish a task) and 動詞+完 (finish doing)
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 完成 + 名詞  /  主語 + 動詞 + 完 + (名詞) + 了
grammar.explanation: 完成 is a two-syllable verb that needs an object you can 'accomplish': 一件事、比賽、課. When you just want to say you finished doing some action, put 完 right after the verb: 吃完、看完、玩完. 完 is a result complement, not a main verb.
grammar.contrast: 結束 is the one most easily confused with 完成. 結束 means an event comes to an end and usually has no object (比賽結束了), while 完成 always takes an object and means a person accomplished something (他完成了比賽). If the subject is a thing/event that stops, use 結束; if the subject is a person finishing a task, use 完成.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 我完成吃飯了 or 比賽完成了. Say 我吃完飯了 (verb + 完) and 比賽結束了 (an event ends). 完成 needs a task-like object after it.

passage.title: 比賽的那一天
passage.hanzi: 上個週末，我和朋友一起參加了學校的跑步比賽。那天天氣很熱，我跑得很累，但是我很努力，最後完成了比賽。比賽結束以後，我們去吃了牛肉麵，還玩了一下電腦遊戲。朋友說，下次他想去騎馬，我覺得那也很好玩。
passage.gloss: Last weekend my friend and I took part in our school's running race. It was very hot that day and I got really tired from running, but I tried hard and finally finished the race. After the race ended, we went for beef noodles and played computer games for a while. My friend said that next time he wants to go horseback riding — I think that would be fun too.
